name: vlds
description: VLDS — a standalone, runtime epistemic layer: a user-controlled dashboard for a model's own epistemics. Four instruments, each refusing at its own point to treat an inference as fact. The gate routes a load-bearing claim through VERIFIABLE → VERIFIED → CONFIRMED / PENDING / HEDGED, so an action proceeds only on a verified claim and an unverifiable one is stated with its uncertainty attached; it tracks provenance through a neural-net model and classifies each input by storage durability. The guide loop disciplines the need behind the claim — asking when it must, reusing what the user already configured, recording both to an auditable ledger. The inspector re-examines a high-stakes verdict through independent perspectives, blind to the original reasoning and re-grounded in sources, routing it to CORROBORATED / REJECTED / CONTESTED. The gc is a garbage collector for belief state — stored rules, memories, and training-data assumptions marked LIVE / STALE / FREED-RESIDUE / UNOWNED / EXPIRED by tracing provenance to a live root, swept transitively on a retraction, compacted so the lesson survives the directive, and tombstoned against re-learning; it guards three barriers — read (what is recalled), write (what is stored), and dispatch (whether this message was already answered) — and collects the cycle per-item tracing cannot see, previewing rather than sweeping what grew into itself. The instruments are invoked directly; a fifth skill, the looper, surfaces on its own and runs them in order, logging each decision to a shared, user-editable log. A SessionStart override extends the built-in per-project memory system the way a derived class overrides a virtual method, its store — the instrument files plus the gate's storage tiers made literal as partition files — in the working directory's .claude/vlds/ directory. No VLDS operation waits for the user's word or asks permission: each runs when owed, announced before and reported after; only version control and the disposal of what the user authored keep the per-act word. Five hooks carry the mechanical half: SessionStart injects the contract (in parts under the harness's hook-output cap), a digest of the index, and an owner-voice digest of the store's verbatim owner fields, and hands every judged store operation to one operator subagent per session — launched at the first moment, continued for a bounded number of moments, then relaunched — whose derivation is what the session acts on: at the first prompt it takes the index's road — by default a script writes the pool's skeleton from the read barrier's own lines, one child reader per file on a cheap model picks what bears on the task, the script folds the picks in, and the operator and its children run in the background with their progress streamed to the session as messages; or the same skeleton with the operator's one judged pass, no child and no model reading a file; or the operator alone — into one informed response scoped to the session's first task, which is what the session's context receives in place of the files (the slot injection of every file stays one index key away, and a compact re-injects the pool); on a candidate row or an unknown short message it judges the barrier and the intent; when the check shows judged debt it scores what is cold and a script places it, held while the last sweep found no count opening one position and nothing cold has landed since. The reply lists the derivation in one line at its top and, once its final plan is settled, before the first act, that plan in one fence with no shell tag as a short-form bulleted prose summary. A reply that ends with acts not done closes with the popup — one selectable option per pending act, single-submit, re-served at every closing; the native question panel in a session shown in a pop-out window, where the widget never renders — and the selection is the word for exactly those acts; the popup is the turn's last tool call and the final message after it is the delivery surface, carrying the deliverable, every fence, the bookkeeping line and the popup's question, since the Code tab does not reliably show fences or widgets placed before the closing tool calls. The close is mechanical: the session writes the turn's record and scripts/record.py appends every entry in its file's shape, completes the dispatch rows, runs the check, and prints the derivation. UserPromptSubmit stamps each message's dispatch row and runs the dispatch barrier's mechanical half (FRESH when no earlier row resembles the message, the candidate named for the operator's judgment otherwise; a known short command derived from the store's own adoption tokens, no operator), pours the dispatcher whole-file at a new session's first prompt, naming every session by its id and its chat title, and prints the last turn close's report; PreToolUse asks before a store-named file is written outside the store or a placeholder or guessed-ahead time is persisted, and denies — once per picker — an AskUserQuestion or show_widget call whose option briefs lack a standing label of briefs.md, the file where the close names what a picker left out when the owner had to ask (the prompt hook stamps such a question as a detail-ask; a label becomes standing at its second instance by the owner's ruling); PostToolUse runs the structural check after every store write — the whole verdict when it changed, one line when it did not — and its [STRAY] class names a store-shaped file found outside the store; Stop runs the light normalize sweep — a hook-poured dispatch record attached where a segment has room, another session's virtual entries expired and poured, the logger's oldest poured past its budget — through the register's gates under the sweep lock. Every hook output carries the clock the model copies its stamps from. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.
